title.narrative: Validating plastic recycling in Senegal and Gambia

description.narrative: Waste collection and processing is a challenge in fast growing urban areas in Senegal and Gambia. Plastic waste often ends up being burned at dumping sites, damaging the environment and increasing public health risks. The global production of plastics is growing rapidly whilst the production and use of recycled plastics is not keeping up with demand. The companies West Africa Plastics B.V. (WAP) and Plastic Recycling Gambia focus on the collection and processing of high quality used plastics from Senegal and Gambia to sell for further processing in the Netherlands (upcycling). Senegal already has a small plastics recycling industry, whereas for Gambia this market is entirely new. Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provides support to validate commercial viability of collection, processing and shipping of 175,000 kg of shredded plastics from Senegal and Gambia to the Netherlands. The project includes setting up 2 processing facilities in Thiès (Senegal) and Old Yundum (Gambia), selecting reliable partners for the sourcing of plastics and transferring knowledge. The project directly supports 96 jobs of which half involves youth and female employees and contractors who have collectively negotiated flexible working hours at a price per processed kilo which is higher than local standards. The project indirectly supports an additional 78 jobs and enables knowledge transfer by training 26 young people mainly regarding plastic waste sorting and processing and introducing new and improved production processes. Furthermore the project aims to contribute to a circular economy and the institutionalisation of the informal waste sector by creating formal collection points, guaranteeing regular purchase of plastics and by creating a different kind of payment system, which leads to more certainty in the entire plastics chain and improved livelihoods and working conditions for all involved.Further investments in the processing and sorting facilities are currently being explored.
